4477.prule: No stress rule stated in any reachable source. Okpe is described as a tone language: two level tones (High, Low) plus a downstepped High (Omamor 1988 n.6 is unsure whether the third pitch is a downstepped H or a raised L); nouns and verbal nouns carry lexical tone melodies (L-H on verbal nouns from monosyllabic verbs, L-H-L on trisyllabic verbal nouns); verbs have no inherent tone in isolation and take their tones from the syntactic context. Elugbe 1989 adopts Hoffmann's (1973) two tones + downstep. No source mentions stress, accent or prominence (0 hits in all five saved texts).

4477.tone: Tone system, first-hand: Omamor 1988 marks High, Low and a downstepped High ('!') on Okpe forms, following Hoffmann 1973, and states in n.6 that she is not certain whether the third pitch is a downstepped high or a raised low; verbs carry no inherent tone in isolation. Verbal nouns show fixed L-H and L-H-L melodies (p.57). Elugbe 1989 sec. 4.6.8 assumes Hoffmann's two tones + downstep; sec. 3.5 p.48 says SWE languages generally lack downdrift but have downstep in some cases and a final-low-raising phenomenon. Pulleyblank 1986 p.120 n.2 uses H, L and '!' downstep. Rolle 2026 treats Okpe [oke] noun melodies (e.g. H-L where Eruwa has L-H). None of these sources says anything about stress or accent: the word 'stress' does not occur in Omamor 1986/1988, Pulleyblank 1986, Elugbe 1989 (whole book) or Rolle 2026 (checked by a full-text search; the only 'accent'/'prominent' hits are unrelated: accented Yoruba, 'a prominent feature', Ijo pitch-accent references in Blench's bibliography). So the sources establish a two-tone-plus-downstep system and do not discuss stress; no source explicitly denies word stress.

4496.prule: Contrastive, lexically specified stress confined to a two-syllable window at the left edge of the word: primary stress falls on the first or the second syllable according to the lexical stress marking of the roots and affixes in the word (minimal pairs differ only in stress placement, e.g. (35) P3P-count 'to count them' vs VAL-count 'to count things'); the unmarked default position is the second (peninitial) syllable, and when lexical stress lies outside the window primary stress surfaces on the second syllable by default (p. 33). Vowel length is contrastive but plays no role in placement (quantity-insensitive).
4496.srule: Rhythmic: secondary stress on every other syllable after the primary stress -- on the 4th (6th...) syllable when primary stress is peninitial (the default), on the 3rd and 5th when primary stress is initial (lexically marked words); stress always alternates with neither clash nor lapse, and vowel length plays no role (left-to-right quantity-insensitive iambs). Established on words of at most five syllables (fn. 7); no lexical secondary stress assumed (fn. 9).

tn.quote: Le samayé, comme la grande majorité des langues bantoues est une langue à tons. ... Le samayé comptabilise trois registres tonals différents: - Un registre haut, noté H - Un registre moyen, noté M - Un registre bas, noté B. ... Les unités porteuses de tons sont de deux sortes - les voyelles ... - la consonne nasale homorganique syllabique ... [p. 65] Au regard de cette liste on peut conclure à l’existence de seulement deux tons distinctifs en samayé, les tons /H/ et /B/. ... [p. 68] Le ton bas tombant n’apparaîtra pas dans le système tonologique du samayé.
tn.translation: Samayé, like the great majority of Bantu languages, is a tone language. ... Samayé has three different tonal registers: a high register, written H; a mid register, written M; a low register, written B. ... The tone-bearing units are of two kinds: the vowels ... and the syllabic homorganic nasal consonant ... [p. 65] In view of this list one can conclude that there exist only two distinctive tones in Samayé, the tones /H/ and /B/ [L]. ... [p. 68] The low-falling tone will not figure in the tonological system of Samayé.
tn.cite: Mokrani, Soraya. 2005. Eléments nouveaux en vue de la description de la langue samayé (B25): éléments de phonologie et de morphologie. Mémoire de Master 2, Université Lumière Lyon 2 (dir. L. Van der Veen). 150 pp. hdl:11858/00-001M-0000-0012-6A21-F.

tn.note: Two level tones H and L on vowels and the class-3 syllabic nasal; mid and low-falling are phonetic variants. Few stem melodies (H, L, HL, LH, LHL, HLH); downstep from floating L; no spreading.

4502.prule: Fixed final: the basic word accent ('el acento básico de la palabra') always falls on the last syllable; preceding prefix syllables are in an unaccented position, where the prefix vowel a laxes to ä.
4502.srule: Not mentioned in Rupp 2012 (Gramática chinanteca sec. 5.1 p. 254, sec. 4.5 pp. 247-249, front matter 'Los tonos' pp. xi-xii; full-text search of the dictionary). The only word-stress statement is the one-sentence final-stress remark; nothing on secondary or rhythmic stress.
4502.quote: El prefijo läˉ- se combina con un adjetivo y lo convierte en un verbo intransitivo. Es posible que el verbo laꜗ ser, suceder sea la fuente de este prefijo. Puesto que el acento básico de la palabra siempre aparece en la última sílaba, la vocal del prefijo está en una posición que no se acentúa, lo que permite que la pronunciación de la vocal a se “afloje”, es decir, se pronuncie como la vocal ä. [examples:] lle̱ey̱ꜘ ADJ AN enojado / dsaˉläˉlle̱ey̱ꜘ VI AN enojar

4502.tone: Full tone system: 'El chinanteco de Ozumacín puede tener tres, seis o nueve tonos, dependiendo del punto de vista desde el que se analice' (p. xi): three level tones (alto, medio, bajo), each also 'con acento' — ballistic accent, 'la elevación del tono disminuye rápidamente', written with a dot on the tone diacritic — plus three rising tones (p. xii), and tone sandhi across words and before pause ('Reglas morfofonémicas', p. xii). The ballistic 'acento' is a syllable-level property independent of the word stress of sec. 5.1: it occurs on prefixes too (e.g. preterite gaꜙ-, sec. 4.5.1), so it is not what 'siempre aparece en la última sílaba'. Verdict is fixed and quantity-insensitive, not tone or pitch accent, because the source does state a word-stress position; a reviewer may wish to flag that the stress statement is incidental and co-exists with a nine-tone system.

tn.quote: El chinanteco de Ozumacín puede tener tres, seis o nueve tonos, dependiendo del punto de vista desde el que se analice. ... Son tres tonos básicos: alto, medio y bajo. ... Los tres tonos básicos también se presentan con acento, en los cuales, la elevación del tono disminuye rápidamente. ... Se puede pensar que los seis signos presentados hasta ahora representan seis tonos, o bien, son los mismos tonos básicos modificados por el acento. ... Además hay tres tonos que sufren una elevación de la voz a través de la duración de la sílaba.
tn.translation: Ozumacín Chinantec can have three, six or nine tones, depending on the point of view from which it is analysed. ... There are three basic tones: high, mid and low. ... The three basic tones also occur with accent, in which the pitch height drops rapidly. ...
